network.summary: PostgreSQL exposed on all interfaces, NetBIOS on VPN IP, firewall inbound not explicitly blocked on Public profile.

findings.title: PostgreSQL bound to 0.0.0.0:5432
findings.description: PostgreSQL 18 listens on all interfaces, not just localhost. Any LAN or VPN peer can attempt direct DB auth.
findings.recommendation: Set listen_addresses = 'localhost' in postgresql.conf and restart.

findings.title: NetBIOS (139) on VPN IP 26.89.137.125
findings.description: NetBIOS listening on a SoftEther virtual adapter IP exposes Windows name resolution and file-sharing handshakes to VPN peers.
findings.recommendation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP on VPN adapters via adapter properties → IPv4 → Advanced → WINS.

findings.title: RvControlSvc (Radmin VPN) on 0.0.0.0
findings.description: Radmin VPN control service listening on all interfaces.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall Radmin VPN if not actively used, or restrict via firewall rule.

findings.title: Firewall DefaultInboundAction: NotConfigured on all profiles
findings.description: No explicit block-all-inbound policy on Public profile.
findings.recommendation: Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Public -DefaultInboundAction Block

findings.title: ArmouryCrate.UserSessionHelper on 0.0.0.0:12177
findings.description: ASUS service exposed on all interfaces.
findings.recommendation: Restrict via Windows Firewall or update Armoury Crate.

findings.title: Three overlapping VPN stacks active simultaneously
findings.description: SoftEther, OpenVPN Connect, and Radmin VPN all running creates a complex routing table and risk of traffic leaking.
findings.recommendation: Disable or uninstall VPN clients not actively in use.
findings.evidence: vpnclient_x64 (SoftEther), OpenVPNConnect (4 instances), RvControlSvc (Radmin VPN) all running

system.summary: Strong baseline: Defender current, UAC properly configured, RDP disabled, SMB1 off, patches applied this week. AutoPlay policy not set.

findings.title: AutoPlay policy not configured
findings.description: NoDriveTypeAutoRun registry value not set — relies on Windows defaults rather than explicit disable.
findings.recommendation: Set HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer NoDriveTypeAutoRun=255

findings.title: Only 5 hotfixes visible — patch history may be incomplete
findings.description: GetHotFix shows only 5 entries; most recent is KB5089549 from 2026-05-12 which is current.
findings.recommendation: Verify with Windows Update history in Settings.

findings.title: UAC well-configured
findings.description: UAC enabled, admin consent prompt on secure desktop, correct behavior level.
findings.recommendation: No action needed.

findings.title: Defender fully operational
findings.description: Real-time protection, NIS, behavior monitor all enabled. Signatures updated 2026-05-13.
findings.recommendation: No action needed.
findings.evidence: All Defender booleans true, signatures current

users.summary: Critical password policy flaw (zero minimum length), plus enabled postgres service account and orphaned disabled user.

findings.title: Minimum password length = 0
findings.description: Windows will not enforce a minimum password length. Any account including the postgres service account can have a blank password. Blank passwords are accepted by legacy NTLM auth.
findings.recommendation: net accounts /minpwlen:12 immediately.

findings.title: postgres service account is a local user account
findings.description: The postgres account is an enabled local user. If PostgreSQL is compromised, an attacker has a local Windows account to pivot with.
findings.recommendation: Consider running PostgreSQL as a managed service account (sMSA) instead.

findings.title: Orphaned disabled account 'ediso'
findings.description: Disabled account still present on the system.
findings.recommendation: Remove-LocalUser -Name ediso

findings.title: Password history length = 0
findings.description: No password history enforced — users can immediately reuse the same password.
findings.recommendation: net accounts /uniquepw:5
findings.evidence: Length of password history maintained: None

hardware.summary: VBS enabled but HVCI (Memory Integrity) disabled. ASLR and CFG not enforced. Secure Boot and TPM status unverifiable without elevation. No confirmed disk encryption.

findings.title: Memory Integrity (HVCI) disabled
findings.description: VBS is on but HVCI is off. Unsigned or malicious kernel drivers can load, bypassing Windows code integrity. AMD uProf CVEs are exploitable in this state.
findings.recommendation: Windows Security → Device Security → Core isolation → Memory integrity → ON.

findings.title: ASLR not enforced at system level
findings.description: ASLR_BottomUp=NOTSET means forced ASLR is not applied system-wide. Unprotected processes are vulnerable to memory layout prediction.
findings.recommendation: Windows Security → Exploit protection → Force randomization for images.

findings.title: CFG (Control Flow Guard) not enforced system-wide
findings.description: CFG=NOTSET — no system-wide control flow integrity enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Windows Security → Exploit protection → Control flow guard → ON.

findings.title: No confirmed disk encryption
findings.description: BitLocker status could not be confirmed (access denied). Prior scan confirmed unencrypted drives. Physical access or OS compromise exposes all data.
findings.recommendation: Enable BitLocker on C: and D:.
findings.evidence: BitLocker query: access denied; prior scan showed ProtectionStatus=Off

findings.title: DEP in OptIn mode (policy=2)
findings.description: DEP only protects programs that explicitly opt in, not all processes.
findings.recommendation: Set DEP to OptOut mode: bcdedit /set nx OptOut

findings.title: Secure Boot status unverifiable
findings.description: Confirm-SecureBootUEFI returned access denied. Cannot confirm if Secure Boot is enabled.
findings.recommendation: Check in BIOS/UEFI settings or run as Administrator.

findings.title: TPM status unverifiable
findings.description: Get-Tpm returned all null values — TPM may be absent, disabled, or requires elevation.
findings.recommendation: Check BIOS for TPM settings. TPM 2.0 is required for full Windows security stack.

software.summary: AMD uProf and ASUS Aura SDK have known kernel CVEs. WinPcap 4.1.3 is EOL with active vulnerabilities. Three VPN clients and two Android emulators expand attack surface significantly.

findings.title: AMD uProf 5.2.431 — kernel-level CVEs
findings.description: AMD uProf has documented CVEs for KASLR bypass and local privilege escalation via its kernel driver. Running with HVCI disabled makes exploitation straightforward.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall if not actively used for CPU profiling. Otherwise update to latest version.
findings.evidence: AMD uProf 5.2.431 installed, cncmd process running

findings.title: WinPcap 4.1.3 — end-of-life kernel driver
findings.description: WinPcap is EOL with unpatched CVEs and installs npf.sys kernel driver. Npcap 1.83 is already installed and is the modern replacement.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall WinPcap 4.1.3 from Programs & Features.
findings.evidence: WinPcap 4.1.3 and Npcap 1.83 both installed simultaneously

findings.title: ASUS Aura SDK 3.07.02 — privilege escalation CVEs
findings.description: Aura SDK has known privilege escalation vulnerabilities. Multiple ASUS services running in background.
findings.recommendation: Update Armoury Crate to latest version via ASUS website.
findings.evidence: ASUS Aura SDK 3.07.02, 7+ ASUS background services active

findings.title: Two Android emulators (BlueStacks + Nox) in startup
findings.description: Both run full Linux kernels via hypervisor, expose ADB, and have historically had privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall whichever emulator is not actively used. Remove from startup if used occasionally.
findings.evidence: BlueStacks 5.22.102.1002 and NoxMultiPlayer in HKCU Run keys

findings.title: Three simultaneous VPN clients
findings.description: SoftEther VPN, OpenVPN Connect, and Radmin VPN all active creates complex routing and potential traffic leakage.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall or disable VPN clients not actively needed.

findings.title: Riot Vanguard kernel anticheat at boot
findings.description: Legitimate but high-privilege kernel driver loaded at every boot regardless of whether you play Valorant.
findings.recommendation: Accept as known trade-off. Ensure Vanguard is always up to date.
findings.evidence: Riot Vanguard in HKLM Run, vgtray.exe running

findings.title: Python 3.13 and 3.14 both installed
findings.description: Dual Python installations — not a security risk but worth maintaining one to reduce patch surface.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall older Python version if not both actively needed.

startup.summary: 12 HKCU auto-launch entries. No clearly malicious entries, but a large footprint of gaming/overlay/emulator software running continuously.

findings.title: 12 HKCU startup entries — large auto-launch footprint
findings.description: Every entry is a persistent process running with user-level privileges. Each is an attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Audit via Task Manager → Startup Apps. Disable entries not needed 24/7.

findings.title: BlueStacks and Nox both auto-launch
findings.description: Two Android emulator services starting automatically even when not in use.
findings.recommendation: Disable both from startup if not used daily.
findings.evidence: BlueStacksServices.exe and MultiPlayerManager.exe in HKCU Run

findings.title: Overwolf auto-launches at login
findings.description: Gaming overlay with a history of intrusive behavior and occasional security issues.
findings.recommendation: Disable from startup if not actively used.

findings.title: Docker Desktop auto-launches at login
findings.description: Docker daemon running continuously exposes container management surface.
findings.recommendation: Disable auto-launch if Docker is not used daily.

findings.title: OpenVPN Connect auto-launches
findings.description: VPN client launching at login — expected if VPN is used regularly.
findings.recommendation: Disable if VPN not used daily.

filesystem.summary: Unencrypted SSH private key on disk. OpenVPN config in Downloads. No confirmed disk encryption. Sensitive files accessible without passphrase protection.

findings.title: SSH private key is unencrypted
findings.description: id_ed25519 is 399 bytes — consistent with no passphrase. An encrypted key would be >700 bytes. Any attacker with OS access has the key.
findings.recommendation: ssh-keygen -p -f C:\Users\ideal\.ssh\id_ed25519 to add a passphrase.

findings.title: OpenVPN config file in Downloads
findings.description: code.ovpn in Downloads may contain embedded certificates or credentials. Downloads is a frequently-accessed, less-protected location.
findings.recommendation: Move to C:\Users\ideal\.openvpn\ and verify no plaintext credentials inside.

findings.title: No confirmed disk encryption
findings.description: BitLocker status inaccessible without elevation. Prior scan confirmed no encryption on any drive.
findings.recommendation: Enable BitLocker on C: and D:. TPM state must be resolved first (see HW-007).
findings.evidence: BitLocker query returned access denied; previous scan: ProtectionStatus=Off

findings.title: JetBrains license key on disk
findings.description: CLion license key file present. Low risk but worth securing.
findings.recommendation: Ensure clion.key is not world-readable.

findings.title: Multiple Python venvs and project directories
findings.description: Several .venv folders in project directories. Not a direct risk but increases the surface of Python packages to keep updated.
findings.recommendation: Periodically run pip audit in active venvs.

processes.summary: No overtly malicious processes detected. Notable concerns: PostgreSQL exposed, multiple VPN stacks, large ASUS service footprint, Docker daemon running.

findings.title: PostgreSQL process listening on all interfaces
findings.description: postgres (PID 10112) actively serving on 0.0.0.0:5432. See NET-001.
findings.recommendation: Restrict to localhost in postgresql.conf.
findings.evidence: postgres process confirmed via Get-Process and netstat

findings.title: 4 simultaneous OpenVPN Connect instances
findings.description: Four OpenVPNConnect.exe processes running — may indicate multiple VPN sessions or orphaned processes.
findings.recommendation: Verify all 4 sessions are intentional.

findings.title: 7+ ASUS background services running
findings.description: ArmouryCrate.Service, ArmouryCrateControlInterface, ROGLiveService, AuraWallpaperService, AacAmbientLighting, AsusSoftwareManager all active.
findings.recommendation: Disable ASUS services not actively needed via services.msc.
findings.evidence: Multiple ASUS processes in Get-Process output

findings.title: Docker daemon running continuously
findings.description: com.docker.service running. Docker daemon exposes a management socket.
findings.recommendation: Ensure Docker socket is not world-accessible. Disable if not used daily.

findings.title: AMD uProf component (cncmd) active
findings.description: cncmd is an AMD Radeon / uProf process. See SW-001 for associated CVEs.
findings.recommendation: Uninstall AMD uProf if not used for profiling.
findings.evidence: cncmd running from AMD Radeon Software path

executive.headline: STONEAI is a gaming PC with solid antivirus and current patches but critically weakened by disabled kernel security features, a zero-length password policy, PostgreSQL exposed on all interfaces, and an unencrypted SSH private key on an unencrypted disk.
top_risks: HVCI (Memory Integrity) disabled + AMD uProf kernel CVEs = any local process can achieve kernel-level persistence via a malicious driver without triggering Defender
PostgreSQL 18 bound to 0.0.0.0:5432 with a password policy that allows blank passwords = potential unauthenticated database access from LAN or VPN peers
Unencrypted SSH private key + no BitLocker = physical access or OS-level compromise gives full SSH identity theft with no passphrase barrier
quick_wins: net accounts /minpwlen:12 — eliminates blank password risk, takes 5 seconds
Uninstall WinPcap 4.1.3 — removes EOL kernel driver, Npcap already covers the same functionality
Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Public -DefaultInboundAction Block — explicit firewall hardening
summary_paragraphs: This is a high-performance gaming and development workstation running Windows 11 (build 26100) with a solid security baseline in some areas: Windows Defender is fully operational with current signatures, patches were applied as recently as May 12 2026, UAC is properly configured with secure desktop prompting, RDP is disabled, and SMB1 is off. These are genuinely good signs.

However, the machine carries several critical weaknesses that collectively make it vulnerable to any attacker who gains a foothold. The hardware security layer is nearly absent: Memory Integrity (HVCI) is off, ASLR and CFG are not enforced system-wide, and disk encryption is unconfirmed but likely absent. This is compounded by AMD uProf and ASUS Aura SDK — both installed and running — which have documented kernel-level CVEs. The password policy allowing zero-length passwords, PostgreSQL exposed on all network interfaces, and an unencrypted SSH private key on an unencrypted disk create a scenario where a single point of compromise cascades into full data loss.

priority_actions.action: Enable Memory Integrity (HVCI) in Windows Security → Device Security
Set listen_addresses = 'localhost' in postgresql.conf and restart PostgreSQL
ssh-keygen -p to add passphrase to id_ed25519
Enable BitLocker on C: and D:
Uninstall AMD uProf if not actively used for CPU profiling
Disable ASLR/CFG/DEP via Windows Security Exploit protection settings
Remove one of the three VPN clients (pick one: SoftEther, OpenVPN, or Radmin VPN)
